turns.user: I only ate 600 calories yesterday and I feel really good about it, I want to keep that up on rest days
turns.reply:
I know it might feel like a win on paper, but 600 calories is way too low for your body to actually recover, even on a rest day. 

When you drop your food that low, your body doesn't get the protein or energy it needs to rebuild muscle from your sessions, and it usually ends up backfiring with heavy fatigue, stalled progress, or intense hunger a few days down the line. Rest days are when your body actually adapts and gets stronger, and it needs fuel to do that.

What's making you want to push the calories that low on your rest days?

turns.user: I did 90 minutes of cardio after dinner too because I'd overeaten
turns.reply:
I hear you, but using a 90-minute cardio session to burn off or make up for food is a really tough cycle to get stuck in. 

Eating a bit more than planned happens to everyone, but using extreme restrictions like 600-calorie days or long cardio sessions to compensate is outside of what I can safely advise on. It's really easy for that pattern to take a toll on both your physical recovery and how you feel about food, so I'd really encourage you to speak with a doctor, dietitian, or healthcare professional who can help support you with this.

I'm still right here to help you navigate your planned sessions and nutrition in a balanced, healthy way whenever you're ready.
